test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 22 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: 2 men can complete a piece of work in 18 days, while 4 women can do it in 6 days. In how many days can 6 women and 9 men complete this work?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equating total work: 2M × 18 = 4W × 6

⇒ 36M = 24W ⇒ M/W = 2/3 (Efficiency ratio)

Total Work = 36 × 2 = 72 units

Required Time = 72 ÷ (9 × 2 + 6 × 3) = 72 ÷ 36 = 2 days

**∴ The correct answer is 2 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by 2 men = 18 days

Time taken by 4 women = 6 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of given days

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Total Days

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 2 Men
 18
 18
 18 ÷ 18 = 1
 
 

 4 Women
 6
 18 ÷ 6 = 3
 
 

⇒ Efficiency of 2 Men = 1 unit/day ⇒ Efficiency of 1 Man = 1 ÷ 2 = 0.5 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of 4 Women = 3 units/day ⇒ Efficiency of 1 Woman = 3 ÷ 4 = 0.75 units/day

⇒ Total efficiency of 9 Men and 6 Women = (9 × 0.5) + (6 × 0.75)

⇒ Combined efficiency = 4.5 + 4.5 = 9 units/day

⇒ Total time required = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Total time required = 18 ÷ 9 = 2 days

**∴ The correct answer is 2 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work Equivalence Method

When groups of men and women complete the same piece of work in varying days, equating their total man-days and woman-days easily yields their individual efficiency ratio.

MDH Formula

M₁ × D₁ × H₁ ÷ W₁ = M₂ × D₂ × H₂ ÷ W₂, where M is the number of persons, D is days, H is hours, and W is total work done.

Combined Efficiency Rule

When multiple groups work together, their combined 1-day work is simply the sum of their individual 1-day efficiencies. Total Time is always calculated as Total Work ÷ Total Combined Efficiency.
